method: Skin depth is the distance at which current density in a good conductor has decayed to 1/e, about 36.8%, of its surface value. For conductivity sigma, permeability mu = mu0 mur and angular frequency omega = 2 pi f, delta = sqrt(2 rho/(omega mu)) = sqrt(rho/(pi f mu0 mur)) with rho = 1/sigma. The surface resistance of a smooth semi-infinite conductor is Rs = sqrt(pi f mu0 mur rho) = 1/(sigma delta) in ohms per square, so a square of any size has the same RF resistance; five skin depths contain 1 - exp(-5) = 99.3% of the current, which is why plating is often specified as 5 delta. Presets hold 20 C handbook conductivities in MS/m: copper 58.0, silver 63.0, gold 41.0, aluminum 35.4, brass 70/30 16.0 and phosphor bronze 8.7. The conductivity field is authoritative and can be edited for alloys, another temperature or a plated layer. Frequency is converted from Hz, kHz, MHz or GHz and must lie between 1 Hz and 300 GHz; conductivity is limited to 0.01 to 100 MS/m and relative permeability to 1 to 10000. The model assumes a smooth, homogeneous, thick conductor that is non-magnetic unless a relative permeability is entered, so it does not cover films thinner than a few skin depths, surface roughness, multilayer plating, proximity effect in windings, superconductors, or ferromagnetic metals whose permeability varies with frequency and field. Everything runs locally in your browser and nothing is stored or uploaded.

sources.title: Wikipedia, Skin effect: current density in a conductor falls exponentially with depth and reaches 1/e of its surface value at the skin depth delta = sqrt(2 rho/(omega mu)).
Wikipedia, Surface resistivity: the high-frequency sheet resistance of a good conductor is Rs = sqrt(pi f mu rho) = 1/(sigma delta), expressed in ohms per square.
Wikipedia, Electrical resistivity and conductivity: conductivity is the reciprocal of resistivity, and the presets correspond to handbook 20 C resistivities for common conductors.

Balanis, Advanced Engineering Electromagnetics: skin depth and surface impedance follow from the plane-wave propagation constant in a good conductor, with the surface resistance equal to the real part of the surface impedance.
Microwaves101, Skin depth: plating and coating thickness is commonly quoted as several skin depths because current density decays exponentially into the metal.
